analysis:
Both changed files are test-only. NemotronSuperOpenRouterVideoTests.swift (added, lines 1-143) reads committed SDK video resources, checks their SHA-256 (line 53), and exercises ingress, parse, inspect, the prompt, the media plan, frame decode and serving on the tiny installed fixture. It asserts that the ingress quote plus the plan stay within Policy.videoMediaChargeBytes (line 111) and that reserved bytes return to baseline (line 139). It has no network access, no secrets, no production code path and no new attack surface.

NemotronSuperVideoBindingTests.swift changes are: the expected video media charge rises to 4,875,295,228 (head line 168); a new test, oversizeBodyIsMediaTooLarge (head lines 233-243), checks that Binding.Failure.bodyTooLarge maps to code mediaTooLarge with status 400 while invalidInput maps to invalidMedia; and VideoOwner, videoOwner and SuperVideoEvents are widened from private to internal (head lines 361, 376, 514). That widening affects the test target only.

The updated charge value and the ingress-limit and error-mapping semantics imply production changes in the binding and policy that are not in this batch: an ingress bound raised above 8 MiB and a new bodyTooLarge failure mapping. Those production changes need review in their own units, covering the memory reservation/budget accounting that backs availability (a higher per-request video charge, GPU/KV budget exhaustion, and DoS via large bodies), the media_too_large mapping, and the coordinator-side 413 handling. The tests suggest the charges are reserved and released, but the enforcement code is not visible here. No threat-model assumption in the supplied definitions (including T-041) is affected by these test files. I found no regressions in the supplied units.
